newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy mkt sees o/n rate easing slightly.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy mkt sees o/n rate easing slightly.

text.p: The Italian money market continues to expect money market rates to ease slightly over the next one to three months, a study by the Bocconi university research arm Igier showed on Friday.
Over a two year timeframe, the market saw a larger fall in interest rates, according to the study which extrapolates implicit overnight rates in the future from actual market rates.

The implicit overnight rate was seen at 6.95 percent on a one month horizon, unchanged from last week's forecasts and slightly down from an official market close of 7.07 percent on Thursday, the day on which the forecast was based.
Italy's discount rate currently stands at 6.75 percent and the fixed term advances or Lombard rate at 8.25 percent.
On a three month horizon, the implicit overnight rate was seen at 6.75 percent, a shade up from the 6.70 percent seen a week ago but down from 6.78 percent expected a month ago.
On a one year horizon, the implicit overnight rate was set at 6.40 percent, a fraction below 6.44 percent seen a week ago and 6.59 percent one month ago.
Over two years, the implicit overnight rate was 6.65 percent from 6.94 percent for the same timeframe a week ago and 6.96 percent one month ago.

Still on a two-year horizon, the spread between Italy's implicit overnight rate and Germany's implicit overnight rate was forecast at 212 basis points from 232 basis points a week ago and 228 basis points one month ago.
